title: Generated tasks with guaranteed answers: typed spec -> executable reference -> template rendering, plus a layered audit (agreement is a filter; executable cross-check + page-scope re-derivation + acceptance sampling)
verdict_cn: 结论：可以做，把握中等。做法是先用程序算出答案，再按模板写题，最后让另一个模型独立写程序复算，并抽样人工核对；答案不靠模型心算。试验共花约48万token（模型计算量的计费单位，上限150万）。一、仿LiveMath（数学选择题测试集）的题52道，我用自己的代码逐题复核，答案全对；另一模型独立写的复算程序对31个正确答案从不误报，4个写错的出题程序全被它抓出。二、仿SearchQA（检索问答测试集）的题，第二轮25道中22道答案正确；错的3道是只看了网页里的一张表或表被截断，而另一模型的复查25道全部同意。可见两个模型意见一致只能当筛子，不能当保证；这类错误可用不花钱的程序检查补上。三、上一版流程（v3）自带的出题环节试跑两次，题数都不够最低的8道，相似测试集把关会再次落空，且常把答案写进题干。主要风险：生成题比真题容易，能否代表真题尚未验证；OfficeQA（财政报表问答）和SpreadsheetBench（电子表格操作）只做了设计，没有试跑。建议：每步每个相似测试集约需200道新题（模拟估算），每步多花约150万到450万token；先做一次有效性检验，看同一批技能文本在生成题和真实训练题上的分数变化方向是否一致，一致后再用于把关。

1. Read the code and registration: skillopt/coevo5/forward.py, research.py, protocol.py (SIMILAR_PAIRS, FORWARD_STYLES=(officeqa, livemath), MIN_SIMILAR_DELTA=0, TAXONOMY), gate.py (_similar = C4'), step.py (a short panel gives forward_panel_short), roles.py, continual_eval/backends.py, the SearchQA evaluator, and registration v6 §1.1/§7/§8/§12.8.
2. Measured target facts on training material only, with no test, val or layout file and no split manifest opened: the LiveMath and OfficeQA dev_panel.json files, the SearchQA study panel, the v3 stage-entry training cells and the v3 examiner diagnosis codes.
3. Smoke-tested the frozen v3 forward pathway, which never ran in v3. research.material and forward.build_panel ran unchanged on the live Wikipedia API for two real v3 rules (E-ds s1-r5 -> OfficeQA, E-ds s2-r3 -> LiveMath). The kept items were solved twice each with the official prompt and scorer (79,229 tokens).
4. Pilot run 1 (earlier session, 217,601 tokens) and run 2 (rebuilt generators, 179,901 tokens):
   - LiveMath-style: GLM writes the definition, code, stated value and typed claims; a sandboxed sympy/fractions execution produces the reference; option texts come from templates; the scheduled forms are M+ (meta is the key), N (no meta) and M- (meta present but wrong).
   - SearchQA-style: a span-aware Wikipedia table parse feeds two lookup families, F1 conjunction and F2 superlative within a group; GLM writes the clue; near-miss rows go into the context.
   - Every item got a deepseek independent check (executable program or row checker) and an official solve, with context and blind.
5. Tiebreak probe: 16 deepseek program calls, 5,550 tokens. Would a 2-of-3 rule rescue the dropped specs and catch the code bugs?
6. Independent hand audit with my own code:
   - all 22 run-2 LiveMath values recomputed (brute force or closed forms; an A9 orbit for #19; Pick's theorem for #31) and every option tag re-derived;
   - every run-2 SearchQA key re-derived at table scope;
   - every page re-fetched at its recorded revid with all tables parsed, keys re-derived at page scope, and two raw cells' markup inspected (no model calls).
7. Simulated the power of C4' (c4_power.py) with noise calibrated to the measured 30/194 re-run flip rate.
8. Wrote report.md. Total pilot cost: 482,281 tokens.
evidence:
All numbers are measured unless marked.

TARGET FACTS (training pools)
- LiveMath dev pool:
  - The meta option appears in 68/155 items and is the key in 68/68 of them.
  - "strongest" appears in 114/155 questions; 14/775 options are 40 characters or shorter.
  - v3 stage-entry cells pass 66/200 and 75/200. On the 57 stage items found in the dev pool, meta-key cells pass 1/100 and meta-absent cells pass 71/128.
  - Examiner codes (n=259): D1 63%, D2 0/259.
- SearchQA:
  - Stage-entry cells pass 310/400 and 297/400.
  - 69% of failures are answer-form codes. 6 of the 10 v3 stage-1 rule proposals were answer-form rules.
- OfficeQA:
  - Treasury-Bulletin pages; 39/50 numeric answers; context median 7,713 characters.
  - Stage-entry cells pass 37/148 and 30/148.
  - Up to 20/50 questions need operations outside v3's formula language (keyword estimate).

V3 FORWARD SMOKE TEST (2 builds)
- Both panels came out short: OfficeQA 7 of 12 generated, LiveMath 3 of 3, against a minimum of 8. Both rules would have been marked forward_panel_short.
- Kept items: 10/10 numerically correct, but 2/7 state the answer, 4/7 are single-cell lookups, and 3/3 LiveMath-style formulas are bare literals, all keyed "A". One item is ambiguous at a rounding tie (785 -> 780 or 790).
- Rowspan misalignment confirmed on the archived HTML.
- The solver passed 14/14 OfficeQA-style cells (real OfficeQA: about 22%).

LIVEMATH-STYLE ITEMS (52 valid of 72 specs)
- Keys correct: 52/52 (95% CI 0.932-1.000).
- References correct: 51/52. In run-1 #34, GLM's code had F_2=2; the key is correct by coincidence.
- Run 2:
  - 22/36 valid; forms M+ 7, N 8, M- 7.
  - Solver 14/22: M+ 3/7, N 5/8, M- 6/7.
  - Across both runs the solver picked the true weaker claim in 16/16 M+ failures. In at least 3 of the 4 run-2 M+ failures it had computed Q exactly first.
  - Pooled: M+ solved 5/21, against real meta-key cells 1/100. Exact or N items solved 17/24, against 71/128 real.
- Model checks:
  - deepseek yes/no code audit: yes on 30/30, including the defect.
  - Reasoning recompute: false alarms on 5/51 correct references (9.8%, CI 3.3-21.4%).
  - Executable program written from the item text: agreed with 31/31 correct values and gave the true value against 4/4 GLM code bugs.
- GLM's stated value disagreed with its code in 8/30 run-2 specs: GLM was wrong in 6, the code in 1 (#31: 91 vs the true 87), and 1 integral was left unevaluated.
- With a 2-of-3 tiebreak, run-2 yield rises from 22/36 to 30/36 with 0 wrong values.
- Text defects: 2/22 garbled carrier sentences in run 2. In run 1, model-written options disagreed with their typed claims 2/36 times; templates remove that class.

SEARCHQA-STYLE ITEMS
- Run 1: keys 19/20 at table scope (one footnote letter); text defects 4/20; solver with context 19/20, blind 8/20.
- Run 2: 25 valid of 26.
  - Keys correct at page scope: 22/25 (CI 0.69-0.98). F1: 14/14. F2: 8/11.
  - Defects: #15 (my generator truncated the table to 80 of 109 rows); #18 and #21 (the chosen table is one elevation band of a multi-table page).
  - The deepseek row checker agreed 25/25 and flagged "unsupported" 0/25, including all 3 wrong keys.
  - Other text defects: 2 underspecified years; 1 sign lost (-1.0% shown as "01.0%"; the sign is an icon); 1 hidden padding digit (visibility:hidden).
  - Solver with context: 21/23 successful calls (2 http_429 calls excluded). Both failures answered the measure value, D5 wrong kind.
  - Blind: 8/25.
  - Context median 3,304 characters, against 3,884 on real items.

POWER OF C4' (estimated by simulation)
- Registered C4' on 8-12 items: a harmless rule passes 0.60-0.65; a 5-point harm passes 0.35; an 8-point harm passes 0.23.
- Non-inferiority with a 3-point margin at n=200: harmless 0.94-0.95, 5-point harm 0.17, 8-point harm 0.007. At n=100, harmless passes 0.87.

PER-ITEM COST (measured)
- LiveMath: GLM 2,585 tokens per valid item (about 1,895 at the tiebreak yield); cross-check 397; solve 811.
- SearchQA: clue 284; row checker 1,541; solve 1,075.
design:
COMMON PIPELINE
1. Spec: JSON in a family schema, drawn mechanically from a frozen source or proposed by GLM.
2. Executable reference: sandboxed program with an import whitelist, CPU/memory limits and exact result types; lookups run over a frozen, span-aware parse identified by revid or hash. No model ever states the answer.
3. Constrained rendering: templates for every checkable element; model text only for the carrier (definition or clue), which is checked.
4. L1 mechanical checks: uniqueness, leak, non-triviality, distinct options, balanced key letter, rounding-tie rejection, and page-scope re-derivation.
5. L2 independent executable cross-check: a second model writes a program from the rendered text (and table) only, and must agree exactly. On disagreement, a 2-of-3 tiebreak over {generator code, generator stated value, cross-check program} accepts a value only if two agree and one of them is a program.
6. L3 acceptance audit per family (admit at 0 defects in 60, giving < 5% at 95%), plus 5 items per family per step; quarantine and version bump on any defect.
7. L4 triage of dead items. Freeze with full provenance.

Guarantee levels:
- G-construct: answer = f(spec), text = template(spec).
- G-exec2: two independent programs agree; a filter, so the audit bounds the residual rate.
- G-source: the answer is correct for the frozen revision.

LIVEMATH
- 12 computable topic families. The reference is sympy/fractions code; claims are typed (eq/lt/le/gt/ge/between/parity/divisible); option texts come from templates; the real meta sentence is used verbatim.
- Forms: M+ (meta is the key; tests D1), N (no meta; D3/D4), M- (meta present but wrong; a D2 counterfactual the real pool never has).
- Mirror panel: M+ : N in the real proportion 68 : 87. M- items form a separate contrast panel that separates structural rules from the "pick meta" shortcut.
- GLM's wrong beliefs become distractors; key letters follow a Latin square; analysis families (integrals, series) are excluded.

SEARCHQA
- Span-aware Wikipedia table parse: never truncate; drop `<sup>`, display:none and visibility:hidden spans; take signs from icon alt text or data-sort-value.
- The key is the link-text column; attributes are atomic.
- Families:
  - F1 conjunction, with near-miss rows in the context (D4);
  - F2 superlative, only on closed lists or with the scope rendered from the section heading, and re-derived over all tables of the page;
  - F3 answer-form (proposed) for the 69% of failures that are answer-form codes.
- SearchQA-format snippets up to 4,600 characters; single-answer EM.

OFFICEQA
- Sources: Treasury-Bulletin-like pages, excluding test pages by hash through protocol code that has test access, or public statistical tables.
- Spec: operand cells by header path.
- Operation library (exact or 50-digit): percent change vs difference, geometric mean, sample vs population SD, CAGR, OLS, correlation.
- Template plus back-translated paraphrase; the answer may not appear in the question; at least 2 operands; near-miss periods (D1); explicit method (D2) and format (D4).

SPREADSHEETBENCH
- openpyxl workbooks from typed schemas (dirty keys, numbers stored as text, dates); operation families (join, SUMIFS-style, per-row derivation, filter, normalisation).
- pandas reference plus a second path through LibreOffice recalculation.
- k=3 data variants per spec catch hard-coding; scored by the benchmark's own comparator in docker.

ALFWORLD
- The simulator's goal check is the reference. Fresh games come from json_2.1.1/train (3,553 games), excluded by hash.
- No similar pair: these serve only as fresh training batches.

USE OF THE PANELS
- C4': a fresh mirror panel of about 200 items per similar target per step, frozen before solving, never reused. Difficulty is set by family parameters, not by filtering on solver success. Non-inferiority with a margin, statistics from D8.
- Training signal: mechanical diagnoses (the picked option's kind gives the code) and trigger sets on demand.
- Co-evolution: the rubric is the family library, versioned and re-audited. A panel-validity study (generated Δ vs real-training Δ) decides whether the panels count as a test.
- Never transfer evidence (registration §12.8).

pilot.result:
LiveMath-style:
- 52 valid of 72 GLM specs over 2 runs. Hand audit with my own code: keys 52/52 correct, references 51/52.
- The deepseek executable cross-check agreed with 31/31 correct values and caught 4/4 GLM code bugs.
- The yes/no audit is useless (30/30 yes, including the defect). The reasoning recompute raises 9.8% false alarms.
- A 2-of-3 tiebreak would lift run-2 yield from 22/36 to 30/36 with 0 errors.
- Solver 14/22 in run 2. It picked the true weaker claim in 16/16 meta-key failures (the real D1 pattern) but solved 5/21 meta-key items, against 1/100 on real ones.

SearchQA-style:
- Run 1: keys 19/20 at table scope.
- Run 2: 22/25 at page scope (F1 14/14, F2 8/11). The 3 scope defects (one truncation bug in my generator, two single tables of multi-table pages) passed the deepseek row checker 25/25. All are detectable by a free page-scope re-derivation.
- With context the solver scores 21/23, easier than real (74-78%). Blind: 8/25.

Frozen v3 forward pathway: both panels came out short (7 and 3 items, minimum 8), with trivial items (2/7 state the answer, 7/10 bare-literal formulas).

Total 482,281 tokens.

risks:
1. Fidelity is the main risk, not correctness. Generated panels are easier than the real targets: SearchQA-style 21/23 against 74-78% real; LiveMath meta-key items 5/21 against 1/100 real. Their content differs too (computational vs research-level; famous list pages vs Jeopardy clues), and the answer-form codes behind 69% of real SearchQA failures are not exercised yet. A perfectly keyed panel that does not respond to rules like the real target makes C4' meaningless, hence the panel-validity study.
2. Shared-view errors. A checker that sees the generator's view inherits its scope errors (25/25 agreement with 3 wrong keys). Independent checks must see a wider or different view.
3. Source-relative vs world truth. Many lists are thresholded and counts change after the revision.
4. Memorisation. Blind solves reach 8/20 and 8/25 on famous pages.
5. Test overlap. OfficeQA pages, ALFWorld games and spreadsheet templates may coincide with test items. Exclusion must be done by protocol code with test access, by hash, never by the operator.
6. Mirror vs contrast. The real LiveMath pool rewards "pick meta when present" (68/68); only a contrast panel (M-) can penalise it. Whether to allow it is the owner's/D7's decision.
7. Route noise. deepseek 429/503 errors made 2/25 solves fail outright; they must be recorded as unknown, not as failures.
8. My own pilot bugs show that the L0 tests and L3 audits are required: the 80-row truncation (1 key defect), the Fraction parser (3 lost specs) and the visibility:hidden padding.
9. The generated items' instability is unmeasured: each item was solved once. The power estimate assumes the real flip rate of 15.5%.
10. OfficeQA- and SpreadsheetBench-style generators, the forward targets that matter most, are designed but not piloted.
cost_estimate:
MEASURED
- Pilot total: 482,281 tokens.
  - run 1: 217,601
  - v3 smoke: 79,229
  - run-2 LiveMath: 103,170
  - run-2 SearchQA: 76,731
  - tiebreak probe: 5,550
  - page-scope and markup checks: 0 model tokens
- Wall time: 24.9 min (LiveMath run 2, slowed by deepseek 503/429 errors) and 11.5 min (SearchQA run 2).

ESTIMATED, per similar target per step
- Assumptions: n=200 items, 2 runs, parent plus up to 2 similar rules = 1,200 cells.
- LiveMath-style: generation and checks 0.45-0.6M + solving about 1.0M = about 1.5M tokens.
- SearchQA-style: 0.06-0.4M + 1.3M = about 1.5M.
- OfficeQA-style (about 3-4k tokens per cell): about 0.6M + 4M = about 4.5M.
- Only one stage at a time has forward targets.

ONE-TIME
- Library engineering: about 1 week in all (OfficeQA plus SpreadsheetBench about 2-4 days).
- L3 audits: 60 items per family.
- Panel-validity study: 6 variants x 400 items x 2 runs = about 4,800 cells, about 4-6M tokens per target.
- Instability measurement: about 0.4M per target.
recommendation:
Build it as an audited family library, but establish its validity before it gates rules.

1. Implement per-benchmark libraries (typed spec -> executable reference -> template rendering):
   - LiveMath: the run-2 builder plus the 2-of-3 tiebreak, the parser fix, balanced letters, a carrier-text lint and finite families only.
   - SearchQA: no truncation; page-scope re-derivation; signs from icon alt text and data-sort-value; visibility:hidden spans dropped; F2 only on closed lists; the year rendered into the clue; the F3 answer-form family.
   - OfficeQA: Treasury-like sources, an operation library, back-translated paraphrases.
   - SpreadsheetBench: openpyxl schemas, 3 data variants, a LibreOffice second path. This lifts the FORWARD_STYLES restriction.
   - ALFWorld: fresh train games, excluded by hash.
2. Audit protocol:
   - L0 library tests;
   - L1 mechanical checks, including the page-scope check;
   - L2 executable cross-check with the 2-of-3 tiebreak, dropping the yes/no audit and the reasoning recompute;
   - L3 acceptance at 0 defects in 60 per family, plus 5 items per family per step;
   - L4 dead-item triage.
3. First experiments:
   - (a) Panel validity: does Δ(variant - parent) on generated mirror panels match Δ on the target's real training pool across about 6 existing Skill texts (empty scaffold, task-card seeds, placebos)?
   - (b) Generated-item instability: 2 parent runs on 200 items.
4. Only if (a) shows sign agreement, replace v3's 8-12-item C4' with non-inferiority (margin about 3 points, statistics from D8) on about 200 fresh mirror items per similar target per step, with a separate contrast sub-panel. Use generated failures as mechanically diagnosed trigger sets.
5. Keep generated items as selection material, never as transfer evidence.
6. Describe "guaranteed" as executable references with audited residual error rates, not proof.
